newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin gives Gazprom chief nod of support.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin gives Gazprom chief nod of support.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin gave Gazprom chief Rem Vyakhirev a nod of support at the start of a meeting on the Russian natural gas monopoly's long term growth, Russian news agencies said on Wednesday.
They quoted Yeltsin as saying his meeting with Vyakhirev would cover issues including Gazprom's long-term growth plans, activity on foreign markets and work with Russian companies.
"We will do everything so that you and the state have an incentive, and we will discuss our and your areas of strategy," RIA news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying.
Vyakhirev has scheduled a news conference on Gazprom role as supplier to the former Soviet Union for Thursday at 3 p.m. (1100 GMT).
Yeltsin told Vyakhirev he supported Gazprom's policies, the agencies said.
"I support it, support you and your company," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.

Gazprom has recently been forced to pay billions of dollars in federal tax and pension arrears to make up for crippling cash shortfalls in both systems, but Gazprom itself is still owed billions by government and private sector gas consumers.

Government officials including Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov have forced Vyakhirev and Gazprom in general to accept stronger control by the government, which has a 40 percent stake in the company.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin formerly was head of the ministry which became Gazprom.
The Presidential press service confirmed the meeting had begun at 1 p.m. (0900 GMT).
